extracted_factors.Label: Large-scale Plantations
extracted_factors.Description: Large-scale oil palm and timber plantations are responsible for a significant portion of deforestation in Indonesia, particularly during the late 2000s. These plantations are a primary driver of forest conversion to agricultural land.

extracted_factors.Label: Small-scale Agriculture and Plantations
extracted_factors.Description: Small-scale agriculture and plantations, including oil palm, contribute to one-fifth of national deforestation and are the dominant drivers of forest loss on smaller islands.

extracted_factors.Label: Forest-to-Grassland Conversion
extracted_factors.Description: Conversion of forests to grasslands sharply increased following years with significant fires, particularly influencing deforestation rates in Kalimantan.

extracted_factors.Label: Mining Activities
extracted_factors.Description: Mining is an increasing driver of deforestation, although it contributes a smaller proportion relative to plantations and agriculture.

extracted_factors.Label: Regulatory and Policy Interventions
extracted_factors.Description: Government policies such as Indonesia's forest moratorium on new permits for forest conversion have impacted the rate and scale of deforestation.

extracted_factors.Label: Fire-Induced Deforestation
extracted_factors.Description: Periods of intensive fire activity have resulted in increased forest loss and conversion to grassland, impacting both human health and greenhouse gas emissions.

extracted_factors.Label: Biodiversity Loss
extracted_factors.Description: Deforestation leads to significant biodiversity loss, affecting habitat for numerous species endemic to Indonesia's tropical forests.
